in_hebrew.name: בניהו
in_hebrew.meaning: בנו של יהוה, בן יהוה, הבן של אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בניהו הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'בנו של יהוה' או 'בן יהוה'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'בן' שפירושו בן או בנו, ו'יהוה' שפירושו אלוהים. השם בניהו מופיע בתנ'ך ככינויו של אחד מלוחמי דוד המלך, והוא מוזכר בספר שמואל ובספר דברי הימים.

in_greek.name: Βενείας
in_greek.meaning: Υιός του Θεού, παις του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Βενείας είναι ένα όνομα ελληνικό που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'υιός του Θεού' ή 'παις του Θεού'. Το όνομα αυτό αναφέρεται σε έναν από τους πολεμιστές του βασιλιά Δαβίδ στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη και συγκεκριμένα στο βιβλίο του Σαμουήλ και των Χρονικών.

in_latin.name: Benaiah
in_latin.long_meaning: Benaiah est nomen hebraicum quod significat 'filius Dei' vel 'Dei filius'. Nomen hoc in Biblia Hebraica invenitur, designans unum ex bellatoribus regis David, cuius mentio fit in libro Samuelis et Chronicorum.

in_english.name: Benaiah
in_english.meaning: Son of God, God is my son
in_english.long_meaning: Benaiah is a Hebrew name that means 'son of God' or 'God is my son'. The name is derived from the Hebrew words 'ben', meaning son, and 'Yah', a shortened form of Yahweh, meaning God. Benaiah appears in the Bible as one of King David's mighty warriors, mentioned in 1 Samuel and 1 Chronicles. The name signifies spiritual significance, divine connection, and strong faith. In Christian tradition, Benaiah represents courage, loyalty, and devotion to God.

biblical_reference.note: Benaiah was one of King David's mighty warriors and a leader of the Levites.

data.cultural_impact: The name Benaiah, derived from the Hebrew language, holds a significant cultural impact as it is the name of a renowned and powerful warrior from the Old Testament who served under King David in Israel. Benaiah was the son of the fiery, wise and trusted high priest, Eleazar. He is mentioned in many passages throughout the Bible, most notably as a commander leading thousands of soldiers, and for his bravery in taking down the vastly experienced Philistine champion, Eleazar. His name "Benaiah," representing 'Son of the Lord,' conveyed the idea of divinely ordained courage, strength and authority, which would have resonated deeply with the ancient Israelites.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Benaiah holds a great spiritual significance in the Jewish tradition and in Christianity. It emphasizes the essence of God as the ultimate protector and provider, and how His love and strength are present even in the most challenging situations. It highlights the faith and trust in God as a guiding power and refuge. The name Benaiah is a reminder of the blessings and peace that come from being a child of the Lord, and the belief that with God's grace, one can achieve great things and overcome any obstacle. Having a name like Benaiah not only underscores one's faith but also inspires a sense of inner courage and determination to stand firm in faith and face life's battles boldly.

historical_references.reference: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a mighty warrior in the army of King David. He is best known for killing two high-ranking soldiers, Ahishai the Gibeonite and Joab's brother Asahel, in a single battle.

Benaiah the priest was appointed as the high priest in Jerusalem by King Solomon. He is known for his role in the temple construction and for his efforts to maintain the purity of the temple and the priesthood.
